item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.5
item.description:
0.3.5 — Edit a part where you are looking at it

  • Double-click any part on the Exhaust Designer canvas. A small pane opens on the part itself with its own fields — length, diameter, and whatever else that kind of part has. It is the same set of fields as the settings column, wired to the same numbers, so you can type into whichever one you happen to be looking at and the other follows immediately.
  • Warnings stopped eating the settings column. Each one is now a small orange triangle. Hover it and you get the full text, word for word — nothing was shortened, and nothing changed about when a warning appears.

No solver changes. Your simulation results are untouched. 1002 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.4
item.description:
0.3.4 — Put the collector where you want it

  • The collector can be placed. It used to be pinned to one spot the geometry chose for it — the one part you position by eye on a real car was the one part the drawing would not let you move. Drag it on the Exhaust Designer canvas, or type an exact position into the new Place fields in the Collector settings. A Recentre button puts it back.
  • The primaries re-aim and keep the lengths you authored. Moving the collector changes the angle the runners arrive at, never the length you cut. The run downstream follows the collector's exit, so nothing detaches from it.
  • Your simulation results do not change. This is where the part sits, not what it is — verified against the El Presidente reference, which came back bit-identical.

1002 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.3
item.description:
0.3.3 — Housekeeping

Nothing on screen changes. If you are updating from 0.3.1 or earlier, this release also carries everything in 0.3.2 — the Exhaust Designer fixes and the display units that finally stick.

  • The app is called Exhaustism throughout now. It has been called Exhaustism since July, but the project, the build target and the program file inside the app still carried the working name it was given before it had a real one. They do not any more.
  • Your documents, settings and licence are untouched. The identity macOS uses to recognise the app never changed, so nothing had to be re-registered or re-entered.

No solver changes. 987 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.2
item.description:
0.3.2 — The Designer draws what you typed

  • A bend now turns the run. Adding a bend used to draw it as a straight length pointing the same way as the pipe before it, so the only way to see the turn was to drag the end point round by hand — and then retype the angle the drag had just destroyed. The angle you type is the turn you see. Two bends compound: 45° then 45° leaves the run at 90°.
  • The drawing stops moving on its own. Retyping a bend angle re-aims the run instead of only stretching it, and the run can no longer swing sideways because a neighbouring length happened to collapse to zero.
  • Your display units stick. Length, Diameters, Temperature and Pressure survive quitting the app. They never did — the Units tab saved nothing, so every launch quietly put you back on mm, OD, kelvin and kPa.
  • Zoom survives an edit. Deleting a part used to throw you back to the whole-car view. The canvas keeps its scale and stays where you were looking.
  • Delete key. Select a part on the canvas and press ⌦ or ⌦⌦ to remove it. Backspace inside a number field still edits the number.
  • Inches read as fractions. A measurement shows as 2-1/2, not 2.5 — the way it goes on the tube. Anything off a sixteenth is marked ≈, so a rounded number never passes for an exact one. You can still type decimals or fractions. The cut and build sheets gained fraction columns beside the decimal ones, so the export still sorts.

No solver changes. Goldens bit-identical; 986 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.1
item.description:
0.3.1 — The glove stops going deaf

  • The control channel no longer lives beside your project. Commands are read from a fixed folder, ~/Library/Application Support/Exhaustism/ipc, whether or not a document is open. It used to be derived from the open project's path, which made external control conditional on having saved a file — silently.
  • The failure that prompted this: renaming the app changed its bundle identifier, which moved the preferences domain, which orphaned the remembered project path. The app then launched with nothing open and ignored every command sent to it for nine days, while reporting a stale snapshot as live state. Nothing was broken. Nothing said so.
  • State and run events are still written next to your project when one is open — that copy is a record belonging with the run evidence. It simply is not the channel any more, so Save As can no longer disconnect anything mid-session.
  • Silence is now reportable. The state export names the folder the app is actually watching, so tooling can say “this app is listening somewhere else” instead of trusting an old file.

No solver changes. Goldens bit-identical; 939 tests green, zero failures.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.3.0
item.description:
0.3.0 — The audit burn: honest numbers, disclosed fallbacks

  • Design RPM is saved with the design — it was being silently discarded, and the Designer and the Algebraic quick-check each kept a private target (4,500 vs 6,000). One scavengingTargetRPM now, shared by both, persisted. Sound keeps its own separate target — scavenging and sound are different physics at different rpm.
  • Every sweep is stamped with its run conditions — ambient, fuel, throttle and model flags travel with the result and into the CSV export, so two sweeps can be compared honestly after the fact.
  • MCSA ceiling: a preset's measured minimum cross-section area now caps effective valve area. No default is invented — unmeasured presets ship nil and the solver says so. Wide-open goldens are bit-identical to 0.2.1.
  • Fallbacks now disclose themselves: a 6→2 build that solves as a single collector shows a SOLVED AS SINGLE COLLECTOR badge (persisted, exported) instead of quietly answering a different question; merge advice carries a clocking disclosure; plenum advisory added.
  • New diagnostic: intake-port pressure trace per RPM point — the ram sequence is now visible next to the exhaust pulse.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.2.1
item.description:
0.2.1 — Licensing, quality of life, lighter launch

  • License system (offline, no phone-home): install a signed .exhaustlic in Settings ▸ License. The alpha stays soft-gated — nothing locks.
  • Spacebar toggles the pressure-field playhead app-wide, or Live Rev play/stop while that tab is visible.
  • WAV export no longer freezes the app — background synthesis with a real progress bar.
  • Live Rev volume knob, persisted; pure listener gain, the dB numbers never move.
  • Much lighter launch: saved results now load from the project sidecar on demand instead of all at once — typical launch memory drops from ~800 MB to ~220 MB on a large result store. Charts render identically once loaded; project files are unchanged.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.2.0
item.description:
0.2.0 — Part throttle (FEA-1)

  • The throttle is now a real lever, not a hidden slider. New Throttle control in the Intake & Combustion inspector.
  • With the intake model ON: the butterfly is a genuine variable restriction (1−cos θ plate law) feeding each ITB runner — manifold vacuum, trapped mass and the exhaust pulse emerge from the gas dynamics.
  • Without the intake model: an honest manifold-pressure map scales the blowdown seed (documented approximation, help text says which model you get).
  • Live Rev throttle slider restored; part-throttle sweeps supported.
  • New diagnostics: EVO seed pressure and trapped-charge temperature.
  • Wide-open-throttle results are bit-identical to 0.1.1.

item.title: Exhaustism 0.1.1
item.description:
0.1.1

  • Unified Dozo theme across every view.
  • Sound-grade 3.5 mm mesh option (timbre band recovered above 800 Hz).
  • Intake & Combustion inspector (ITB runner + Wiebe closed-cycle).
  • Reverse-cone tip now modeled on full cat/resonator/muffler chains.
  • New sidecar document format: autosave writes ~11 MB instead of 226 MB.
